passages.title: My Family
passages.text: Hi! My name is Noa. I live with my mother, my father, and my little brother. My grandmother visits us every Friday. She always brings cookies, and I feel so happy when I see her. My best friend lives next door. We play together after school almost every day. I am very proud of my family.

questions.q: Who visits every Friday?
What does the grandmother bring?
Where does the best friend live?

passages.title: A Day at School
passages.text: Every morning I wake up, brush my teeth, and get dressed. I usually walk to school with my classmate. My teacher is kind and helpful, and she never gets angry when we make a mistake. At recess, I play with my friends in the yard. I never forget my homework. Today we have a test, but I feel confident because I practiced every day this week.

questions.q: How does she go to school?
What happens at recess?
Why does she feel confident about the test?
choices: Her friend told her the answers

passages.title: My Best Friend
passages.text: My best friend's name is Maya. We are in the same class, and we sit together every day. Maya is very funny, and she always makes me laugh. When I feel nervous, she helps me feel brave. We collect stickers together, and we love to draw pictures of animals. On weekends, we sometimes have a sleepover at my house or at hers.

questions.q: What does Maya do that makes the writer happy?
What do they collect together?
What do they do on weekends?

passages.title: A Rainy Day
passages.text: It is cloudy and rainy today, so we cannot play outside. My mother says it's a perfect day to stay home. I wear warm socks and drink hot chocolate. My little brother is a little sad because he wanted to ride his bike, but I tell him we can build a puzzle together instead. Later, the rain stops, and a rainbow appears in the sky. We run outside with our umbrellas, just to see it better.

questions.q: Why can't they play outside?
What do the children do instead?
What appears after the rain stops?

passages.title: My Weekend Hobbies
passages.text: On weekends, I love to try new hobbies. On Saturday morning, I like to draw pictures of my favorite animals, especially cats and butterflies. In the afternoon, my family usually goes swimming at the pool near our house. On Sunday, I practice dancing in my room, even though I am still a little shy to dance in front of other people. My father says practice makes you more confident, and I am starting to believe him.

questions.q: What does she draw on Saturday morning?
Where does the family go on Saturday afternoon?
How does she feel about dancing in front of others?

passages.title: Dinner at Grandma's
passages.text: Every Friday evening, my whole family has dinner at my grandmother's house. The food always smells delicious before we even sit down. We usually eat soup, chicken, and a lot of vegetables, and there is always a sweet dessert waiting for us. My grandmother has a special recipe for chocolate cake that everyone loves. After dinner, the grown-ups talk while the children play games in the living room until it's time to go home.

questions.q: When does the family have dinner at grandma's?
What does grandma have a special recipe for?
What do the children do after dinner?

passages.title: My Favorite Animal
passages.text: My favorite animal is the butterfly. It is a beautiful creature with colorful wings, and no two butterflies look exactly the same. Butterflies live near flowers, in forests, and in gardens all around the world. In spring, I like to sit outside and watch them fly from flower to flower. Sometimes a butterfly lands on my hand, and I feel so excited that I almost forget to breathe. Wild animals are truly amazing to learn about, and butterflies taught me to look closely at small, beautiful things.

questions.q: What is special about butterfly wings?
Where do butterflies live?
How does she feel when a butterfly lands on her hand?

passages.title: The Brave Little Bird
passages.text: Once there was a small bird named Pip. Pip lived in a nest high in a tall tree, and she loved her home. But Pip was afraid to fly. Every day, her mother would say, "Pip, it's time to try," but Pip felt too nervous and stayed in the nest. One windy morning, a strong gust of wind pushed the nest, and Pip had no choice — she jumped. For a moment she fell, scared and silent. Then, without even thinking, she opened her wings. She was flying! Pip laughed with joy as she soared over the forest. From that day on, Pip understood something important: sometimes you don't feel brave before you try something new — you feel brave because you tried.

questions.q: What was Pip afraid to do?
What made Pip finally jump from the nest?
What did Pip learn at the end of the story?
choices: You feel brave because you tried
